findings.summary: P1-B: B-joint shows no perturbation-identity use and is 21x worse than the no-change reference on its own anchors; interface adaptation at 1e-4 recovers source reconstruction (900 -> 33) but never beats no-change on held-out conditions and worsens on Jurkat with more source training.
P1-A: explicit gene-specific PCA8 slopes raise validation residual Pearson 0.05 -> 0.13, matching Tx1 PCA8-ridge; B-joint R adds no detectable gain under the two tested heads.
H1 insufficient interface adaptation (new basal encoder at STATE LR 1e-6 in P0) and H2 representation mismatch at STATE's hidden-space basal skip are priority mechanisms; neither is isolated.

Run P1-C in tiers: Tier 0 analysis of existing exports (bias decomposition, matched-coverage references, anchor scale audit, cross-context Pearson guard); Tier 1 native functional check; Tier 2 LR isolation at 1e-6/1e-5; Tier 3 interface variants V1 null-subtracted residual, V2 native basal + zero-init Tx1 conditioning, V2-null control, V3, each with leave-one-anchor-out; Tier 4 A2 head-seed stability.

predicate.primary_metric: held-out-context response loss ratio to no-change, LOAO mean, lower is better
predicate.keep: internal-val ratio < 1 on >= 2/3 anchors (CI excl. 0) AND LOAO held-out ratio < 1 (CI excl. 0) AND identity advantage > 0 (CI excl. 0)
predicate.verify: hpc/run.sh p1c compare -> p1c/comparison/summary.csv with per-(variant, fold) rows and a kept boolean
predicate.ceiling: 7 training units; plateau after two consecutive discards following a keep

config.task: Design the next P1 diagnostic round isolating interface and basal-reconstruction failures
